fields.title: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (GORD)
fields.bodyHtml:
Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (GORD): advanced treatment in Israel

Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease is a chronic condition in which the contents of the stomach regularly return into the oesophagus, causing heartburn and discomfort. Modern approaches to diagnosing and treating GORD are available in Israel, aimed at reducing symptoms and improving patients' quality of life.

Diagnosis of GORD:

  1. Endoscopy:
    Allows the doctor to examine the lining of the oesophagus and stomach for damage or inflammation.
  2. Oesophageal pH monitoring:
    24-hour monitoring of pH in the oesophagus to assess how often and for how long acid reflux occurs.
  3. Oesophageal manometry:
    Assessment of the motor function of the oesophagus and the work of the lower oesophageal sphincter.
  4. Barium X-ray of the oesophagus and stomach:
    Used to image the anatomy of the oesophagus and identify abnormalities that contribute to reflux.

Methods of treating GORD:

  1. Conservative treatment:
    • Lifestyle changes: raising the head of the bed, avoiding late meals and avoiding foods that trigger reflux (fatty and spicy food, caffeine, alcohol).
    • Drug therapy: the use of proton pump inhibitors and antacids to reduce the acidity of the stomach contents and protect the lining of the oesophagus.
  2. Surgical treatment:
    • Nissen fundoplication: an operation in which the upper part of the stomach is wrapped around the lower part of the oesophagus to strengthen its sphincter and prevent reflux.
    • Minimally invasive methods, such as transoral incisionless fundoplication (TIF) and the LINX magnetic device fitted around the oesophagus.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • An individual approach: treatment is chosen according to the severity of symptoms, the patient's way of life and the response to initial treatment.
  • Interdisciplinary medical teams: gastroenterologists, surgeons and dietitians work together to provide comprehensive care.
  • Access to the newest technologies and medicines: the use of modern methods of diagnosis and treatment, including advanced surgical techniques and pharmaceuticals.

Treatment of GORD in Israel is aimed at achieving lasting remission, preventing complications and improving patients' quality of life through a comprehensive and individually chosen approach.

fields.title: Haemangioma
fields.bodyHtml:
Haemangioma: advanced treatment in Israel

A haemangioma is a benign tumour arising from blood vessels. It is most often seen in children as a mark on the skin, but it can also appear in adults and affect the internal organs. In Israel, patients with a haemangioma are offered a comprehensive approach to diagnosis and treatment, including modern methods of assessment and individual treatment strategies.

Diagnosis of haemangioma

  1. Physical examination and history
    The doctor assesses the nature and position of the growth and gathers information about how it has grown and any symptoms.
  2. Ultrasound examination
    Helps assess the structure, size and depth of the growth and its relationship to the surrounding tissue.
  3. MRI or CT
    Used for detailed imaging of haemangiomas located in deeper tissue or in the internal organs.
  4. Biopsy
    Rarely needed, and only where it is necessary to rule out a malignant growth.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)

Treatment of haemangioma

  1. Observation
    Many haemangiomas in children shrink on their own, so where there are no symptoms observation may be recommended.
  2. Drug treatment
    Propranolol and other beta blockers are used successfully to reduce the size of a haemangioma.
  3. Laser therapy
    Effective for superficial haemangiomas, reducing their size and improving their appearance.
  4. Surgery
    Recommended where the haemangioma causes functional problems, pain or cosmetic concerns.
  5. Sclerotherapy
    Injection of an agent into the growth that causes it to scar and shrink.

Why patients choose Israel

  • Highly qualified specialists
    Israel has doctors of international standing with extensive experience in diagnosing and treating haemangiomas.
  • An individual approach
    Every patient is given a personalised treatment plan that takes account of all aspects of their health and the particular features of the growth.
  • Advanced technology
    The use of modern equipment and innovative treatments ensures effectiveness and minimal risk.
  • A comprehensive approach
    Israel gives close attention not only to treating the growth but to supporting patients, including rehabilitation and psychological help.

Treatment of haemangioma in Israel gives patients access to high-quality medical care, modern treatments and comprehensive support at every stage of therapy, which helps them recover quickly and improves their quality of life.

fields.title: Haemorrhoids
fields.bodyHtml:
Haemorrhoids: advanced treatment in Israel

Haemorrhoids are a condition in which the veins around the rectum and anus become inflamed and swollen, leading to pain, bleeding and discomfort. Israeli clinics offer a comprehensive approach to treating haemorrhoids, using modern medical technologies and methods to minimise discomfort and improve patients' quality of life.

Diagnosis of haemorrhoids:

  1. Proctological examination:
    Includes visual examination and palpation of the anal area to assess the state of the veins.
  2. Anoscopy:
    The use of an anoscope for detailed examination of the inside of the anal canal and rectum.
  3. Colonoscopy:
    May be recommended to rule out other conditions of the colon and rectum, particularly where there is bleeding.

Methods of treating haemorrhoids:

  1. Conservative treatment:
    • Drug therapy: the use of local anaesthetics, venotonic agents, anti-inflammatory preparations and treatments that promote healing.
    • Lifestyle changes: a high-fibre diet to make bowel movements easier, increased fluid intake and regular exercise.
  2. Minimally invasive procedures:
    • Sclerotherapy: injection of a sclerosing agent into the haemorrhoid to shrink it.
    • Infrared coagulation: the use of infrared light to cauterise and shrink haemorrhoids.
    • Rubber band ligation: placing bands around the base of the haemorrhoid so that it withers and falls away.
  3. Surgical treatment:
    • Haemorrhoidectomy: surgical removal of the haemorrhoids; used in difficult cases or where other methods have not worked.
    • Transanal haemorrhoidal dearterialisation: a newer procedure in which the blood supply to the haemorrhoids is blocked, causing them to shrink.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • A personalised approach: treatment is chosen individually for each patient according to the stage of the condition and the symptoms.
  • Use of advanced treatments: innovative procedures and technologies make treatment highly effective and keep the risk of complications to a minimum.
  • Comprehensive follow-up after surgery: patients receive advice on diet, lifestyle and managing symptoms to prevent recurrence.

Treatment of haemorrhoids in Israel is aimed at improving patients' condition quickly and removing the underlying causes, which allows lasting remission and a better quality of life.

fields.title: Hydronephrosis
fields.bodyHtml:
Introduction

Hydronephrosis is a serious kidney condition marked by swelling of the renal calyces and pelvis, caused by an obstruction to the flow of urine. It can arise from blockage of the ureters, stones, tumours, congenital abnormalities or other problems that prevent urine draining normally from the kidney. If hydronephrosis is not detected and treated in good time, it can lead to serious consequences, including deterioration of kidney function and the development of chronic renal failure.

Methods of diagnosis

Diagnosing hydronephrosis is an important step in ensuring effective treatment. Several methods allow doctors to establish the presence and degree of hydronephrosis precisely:

  • Ultrasound of the kidneys: one of the most accessible and safest ways of diagnosing hydronephrosis. Ultrasound allows doctors to see the structures of the kidney and establish whether the renal calyces and pelvis are dilated.
  • Computed tomography (CT): CT scanning produces more detailed and precise images of the kidneys and urinary tract. It is particularly useful for establishing the cause of hydronephrosis, such as stones, tumours or congenital abnormalities.
  • Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI): may be used for further study of the kidney structures and to obtain detailed images without radiation.
  • Urography: an X-ray method in which a contrast medium is introduced into the urinary tract to identify obstruction of the ureter and establish the degree of hydronephrosis.

Methods of treatment

Treatment of hydronephrosis depends directly on its cause and severity. In some cases, where the obstruction is minor, it may resolve on its own. Whenever hydronephrosis is diagnosed, however, a qualified medical specialist should always be consulted to determine the best approach to treatment. The main treatments are as follows:

  • Drug treatment: in some cases hydronephrosis is caused by inflammation or infection. Antibiotics or anti-inflammatory medicines may then be prescribed to remove the cause.
  • Widening the ureter: where the ureter is narrowed, an intervention may be carried out to widen the path for urine to drain.
  • Removal of stones and tumours: where stones or tumours are the cause of hydronephrosis, surgery may be needed to remove the obstruction.
  • Drainage of the renal calyces and pelvis: in some cases doctors may fit a temporary drain to ease the flow of urine and reduce pressure in the kidneys.

Advantages of treatment in Israel

Israel is known for its advanced medical equipment, its high level of technology and its experienced specialists. Treating hydronephrosis in Israel offers a number of advantages:

  • Medical innovation: Israel takes an active part in medical research and development. The most modern methods of diagnosing and treating hydronephrosis are available here.
  • An interdisciplinary approach: doctors in Israel often work across disciplines, which supports comprehensive care for patients with hydronephrosis. Clinical teams bring together urologists, nephrologists, surgeons and other specialists to provide the best possible treatment and care.
  • Experienced specialists: doctors at Israeli medical centres have high professionalism and many years of experience in treating hydronephrosis and other conditions of the kidneys and urinary tract. They are trained at leading medical institutions and continually develop their skills and knowledge.
  • Infrastructure and equipment: medical centres in Israel are equipped with advanced technology for accurate diagnosis and innovative treatment. This improves outcomes and reduces the risk of complications.
  • An individual approach: doctors in Israel aim to treat every patient individually. They take account of the particular features of the condition, the patient's general health and their personal needs in drawing up the best treatment plan.
  • Support at every stage: Israeli medical centres provide comprehensive support to patients throughout treatment. Coordinators help with travel arrangements and interpreting and provide the information patients and their families need.

Conclusion

Hydronephrosis is a serious kidney condition that requires timely diagnosis and treatment. With modern methods of diagnosis and advanced treatment, patients have an excellent chance of overcoming it. Israel, with its advanced medical infrastructure and experienced specialists, offers high-quality treatment for hydronephrosis, giving patients the best chance of restoring their health and quality of life.

If you suspect hydronephrosis or have other kidney problems, it is important to seek medical help as soon as possible. Remember that early detection and treatment lead to better results and prevent possible complications.
